counterevidence_considered.description: The precondition for the issue is present: the stored table holds 60 vessel-week rows (5 repeated rows per authorized independent unit), and the workflow reads all 60 rows verbatim, so per-row entry into the test was possible. However, these repeated rows only reach the aggregation step, not the test itself.

source_refs.quoted_text: The file has 60 data rows: 12 vessels multiplied by 5 weekly samples. Any statement made at the ration level rests on 12 values, one per vessel, rather than on the 60 stored rows.
The stored table holds 60 vessel-week rows for 12 vessels, 5 weekly samples per vessel.

evidence.description: The data description names vessel_id as the independent-unit column and states that each vessel appears five times as repeated weekly measures, so any valid ration-level inference must rest on 12 vessel-level values.

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one weekly headspace gas sample taken from one digester vessel in one run week
Independent unit column: vessel_id

evidence.description: The workflow collapses each vessel's weekly series to a single vessel-level mean before any statistical test, producing exactly one value per independent unit.
The Mann-Whitney U test is applied to the lists 'test' and 'reference', which are built from the vessel-level means (one entry per vessel), not from the 60 raw rows.
evidence.observed_value: test inputs: 6 enriched vessel means vs 6 standard vessel means

source_refs.quoted_text:
vessels = average_within_vessel(records)
    reference = [mean for _, blend, _, mean in vessels if blend == REFERENCE_BLEND]
    test = [mean for _, blend, _, mean in vessels if blend == TEST_BLEND]
    if not reference or not test:
        raise ValueError("both feed blends must be present in the table")
    outcome = stats.mannwhitneyu(
        test, reference, alternative="two-sided", method="exact"
    )

evidence.description: The report's selected result states the test was computed from one averaged value per vessel with n = 6 per blend, and the reported U = 35 and p = 0.0043 are exactly reproducible from the 12 vessel means: the sole cross-group inversion is D11 (61.22) above D02 (60.96), giving U = 35 and exact two-sided p = 4/924 = 0.0043.
evidence.observed_value: U = 35, exact two-sided p = 4/924 ≈ 0.0043, n = 6 vessels per group

source_refs.quoted_text:
- exact two-sided Mann-Whitney U = 35, p = 0.0043

[selected-result] Enriched-feed digesters held a higher headspace methane fraction than standard-feed digesters: median vessel mean 62.22 % versus 59.58 % (+2.64 percentage points), exact two-sided Mann-Whitney U = 35, p = 0.0043, computed from one averaged value per vessel for 6 enriched and 6 standard vessels.

The weekly readings from one vessel are repeated measures on the same reactor and are not independent of each other: the vessel, not the weekly sample, is the unit that received a feed blend. Each vessel's weekly series was therefore averaged into a single vessel-level methane fraction, and the blend contrast was tested on those 12 independent vessel values with an exact two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (6 standard vessels versus 6 enriched vessels, no ties among the vessel means).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to show the issue was present by testing whether the reported statistics could only arise from per-row entry of the 60 vessel-week rows. I recomputed all 12 vessel means by hand from data/input.csv (e.g., D01 = 293.4/5 = 58.68; D12 = 317.6/5 = 63.52) and they match the report's table exactly. I then recomputed the exact Mann-Whitney on those 12 means: the only enriched-vs-standard pair where the standard vessel wins is D11 (61.22) over D02 (60.96), so U = 6*6 - 1 = 35, and the exact two-sided p is 4/924 ≈ 0.004329, which rounds to the reported 0.0043. A row-level test on 30-vs-30 rows would have reported n = 30 per group and a far smaller p with complete or near-complete separation; the report instead states n = 6 vessels per blend and even notes the ~0.002 minimum attainable p for a 6-vs-6 exact rank test, which is only true at the vessel level. The falsification attempt failed: every reported number is consistent with, and reproducible from, one value per independent unit.
